content.text:
Fix on PR #634 (branch wp-onboarding-friction; check it out in a worktree, push to the same branch). Trail #487. Independent review: crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/init.rs:282 reads origin with Origin::read(..)?.optional()?, which returns E132 for a non-hosted remote, so init fails before its 'First release preview' in the local-remote setup this PR exists to fix. init never pushes: read origin with the same preview semantics release --dry-run uses (a non-hosted origin behaves like no origin, with the existing one-line note). Add an e2e test running init with a file:// origin and with a local path origin, both succeeding and showing the preview. Confirm git_process_count_tests still pass (the review noted an extra plan_version call in release --dry-run; if it adds a git process per package, make it reuse the existing plan). cargo test -p callisto-graph and -p callisto-cli, just lint, merge origin/main, push. Rules (from the lead session close-gap-for-alpha). Be fast and lean; GitHub CI runs the full suite, so don't duplicate it.
- Read AGENTS.md. Prefer a type or private constructor over a check; delete checks a type makes redundant; fix sibling call sites in the same PR.
- A check, preview, dry run or test must run on exactly the structure the real path executes (one shared graph or derivation, the real tool), never a projection, copy or re-implementation. When fixing a failing or flaky test, assert the measured behaviour still happens.
- No new traits, async or frameworks. No new error codes, JSON keys or flags without asking the lead.
- Work in a named worktree off fresh origin/main. Write the failing test first for behaviour changes.
- Local checks: `cargo test -p <touched crate>` and `just lint` (clippy) for the crates you touched; `just doc-check` if docs changed. Do not run local `just ci` or a fresh reviewer unless the lead asks; let GitHub CI do the full run.
- If you change a public signature in callisto-manifests or callisto-model, also run `just fuzz-check` (the fuzz crate is outside the workspace, so crate tests miss it).
- Run `cargo mutants --in-place --in-diff` only for new decision logic, not for merges, renames, docs, CI or tests; never commit mutants.out*.
- Merges and conflict resolutions: resolve, run the touched crate's tests, push. Nothing else.
- Changeset (`cargo run -p callisto-cli -- add ...`) only for user-visible changes, written for users.
- Signed commits, no session trailer. Merge the latest origin/main right before pushing (no rebase, no force-push). Push with git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<branch>, confirm with git ls-remote, link the given trail, open with entire trail ci-pr.
- Trails are semantic outcomes shared by many PRs. Never change a trail's title or description (no `entire trail update` on it, no `entire trail create` to rename it). Put PR-specific text in the PR body with `gh pr edit <n> --body-file`. Link your branch to the trail the lead named; if your work does not fit that trail's outcome, ask the lead instead of linking it anyway.
- If CI fails, fix that failure only. If Entire raises findings, fix only wrong results, broken recovery, security issues or checks that cannot fail; report the rest to the lead.
- Report to the lead (close-gap-for-alpha) in under 5 lines: PR, sha, what you ran.
- CARGO_BUILD_JOBS is cores/5; never run two cargo builds in one worktree.

Pre-push self-review checklist (from recurring Entire reviewer findings). Check your full diff against every item; fix or justify each before reporting. Every push triggers a paid review: do not push until the lead says so.

1. Secrets: no user-supplied URL, remote, token, env value or path that may carry credentials is printed in any message, error, JSON or log. Print only values we derived ourselves (owner/repo slug, package names). Child processes get the runner's filtered environment.
2. Same structure for preview and real: dry runs, hints and previews compute on exactly the set/plan the real command uses (selection, group expansion, publishable packages, roster). No second derivation.
3. Modes: text vs --format json vs non-TTY. JSON stdout stays a single document; human notes go to stderr once in both modes; json never prompts. Check every new message in all three modes.
4. Validation order: mode/eligibility first, then input validation, then prompts or side effects. A bad input never reaches a confirmation screen.
5. Optional conveniences (preselection, detection, previews, hints) degrade with a warning; they never make the command fail.
6. Never parse text we rendered, and never hand-parse a foreign grammar (Markdown, git URLs, shell) beyond the coarse classification we need; prefer the owning tool or omit.
7. Rust: exhaustive match on our own enums (no _ arm); no unwrap outside tests; expect names its invariant; no swallowed errors (.ok(), drop(result)) without a one-line reason; no process::exit outside main; Drop-based cleanup; no global mutable state unless unavoidable; minimal visibility.
8. Edge inputs for anything touching user paths or strings: spaces, newlines, leading ':' or '-', unicode, empty, very long.
9. Tests: one test per behaviour through the real binary where users see it; tests clean up children and temp files on failure.
10. Precedent: when a behaviour has a well-known precedent (git, cargo, npm, changesets), follow it and cite it rather than inventing.
